description: Give freely and become more wealthy. Be stingy and lose everything. One of those upside-down truths that only makes sense in God's economy.

verse: "Give freely and become more wealthy; be stingy and lose everything."
body_html:
This is one of those upside-down truths that only makes sense in God's economy.

The world tells us to hold on. Keep what is ours. Protect our resources. Look out for ourselves first. And it makes sense on paper. If you give things away, you have less. If you hold on to what you have, you keep more.

But God says the opposite.

Give freely and become more wealthy. Be stingy and lose everything.

I do not think this is just about money. I think it is about a whole way of living. A posture. Because the same principle plays out in almost every area of life.

The person who gives their time freely ends up with a richer life than the person who guards every minute. The person who gives their love away without holding back experiences more love than the one who keeps their heart protected. The person who serves others generously ends up more fulfilled than the one who spends their life on themselves. The person who forgives freely walks in more peace than the one who holds every offense.

Generosity multiplies. Stinginess shrinks.

That is just how God designed it.

I have watched this in real life. The most generous people I know are also the most joyful, the most peaceful, the most alive. They give money, time, attention, encouragement, hospitality, prayer. They give freely. And they always seem to have more, not less. More friends. More opportunities. More laughter. More depth.

And I have watched the flip side too. People who hold on tight to everything they have. Their money, their time, their affection, their approval. And they end up smaller for it. Not richer. Just tighter. Losing exactly what they were trying to protect.

Because a life closed off from giving is a life closed off from receiving. You cannot open your hand to receive if your fist is closed to give.

God is generous by nature. He gave His Son. He gives grace. He gives good gifts. He gives rain to the just and the unjust. He gives us breath every morning we did not earn. When we live generously, we look more like Him. And when we look more like Him, our lives start to bear the kind of fruit only His way can produce.

I want to be that kind of person. Not clenched. Not stingy. Not always calculating what something will cost me before I give it. Just open. Free. Trusting that God will keep filling what I keep pouring out.
question: Where in your life are you being stingy in a way that is actually costing you more than it is protecting you?
